newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds face another tough week afer slipping Friday.
newsitem.headline: Bunds face another tough week afer slipping Friday.

text.p: Bunds face another difficult week starting Monday with worries about U.S. interest rates expected to pull global debt markets lower.
Analysts said that although Bunds may be able to outperform their U.S. counterparts, hints that the German economy may be starting to pick up should limit the German market's relative performance.

As with much of the week, Bunds closely followed Treasuries on Friday, pulled lower by the U.S. market after the release of U.S. jobs data in the afternoon. At 1441 GMT, the DTB June Bund futures contract was down seven basis points at 99.15.
"The bias is still clearly downward given the backdrop of the U.S. market," said Timo Klein, analyst at MMS International in Frankfurt. "In view of the last week, Bunds are in a corrective mode."
Analysts said they expected the Bund/T-note spread next week to remain roughly around 100 basis points, especially ahead of German jobs data due Tuesday.
Bunds closely tracked Treasuries after the jobs data release with the spread ticking up only slightly to around 97 basis points compared with 96 at the close on Thursday.

The major event of early next week will be German unemployment data for March due on Tuesday morning. Economists expect the data to show a decline after climbing 5,000 on a seasonally adjusted basis to 4.316 million in February.

Analysts said the decline could "fool" some people into thinking that the German economy was starting to create more jobs. Although unemployment may indeed dip they said, the overall trend toward higher joblessness should remain through the autumn. The Bundesbank should give the market little distraction during the week with only council member Klaus-Dieter Kuebacher holding speech on Thursday.
Technical factors are also weak. Bunds closed the day below the 99.46 200-day moving average, a sell-signal for some chartists. Support, however, is seen at 98.89 and 98.50.
The yield curve continued to steepen on Friday, with the spread between two and 10-year maturities adding two basis points to hit 236 basis points.
The benchmark 10-year Bund fell by late in the afternoon to 99.69 from 99.75 to yield 6.03 percent.
